brief_title: Effects of Tirzepatide on Corneal Nerve Morphology and Other Ocular Parameters in Adults With Obesity
official_title: Effects of Tirzepatide on Corneal Nerve Morphology and Other Ocular Parameters in Adults With Obesity
brief_summary: This study investigates the effects of a dual glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) and glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) receptor agonist, tirzepatide, on corneal nerve morphology and other ocular parameters in adults with obesity. Participants, adult patients with obesity, will receive either tirzepatide or placebo over 24 weeks. Researchers will assess ophthalmological clinical status, corneal nerve changes, ocular surface, intraocular pressure, anterior-segment biometry and optical coherent tomography, and exophthalmometry. Orbital MRI will be performed in a subgroup of participants receiving tirzepatide. Optical coherence tomography and Optical coherence tomography angiography will be preformed to asses the posterior segment. The goal of this study is to investigate the effects of tirzepatide on corneal nerve morphology and functional consequences, as well as anterior segment parameters, during tirzepatide-induced weight loss, addressing an important gap in understanding the impact of incretin-based therapies on corneal nerves and anatomy of anterior eye segment.

eligibility.criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* BMI between 30 kg/m² and 45 kg/m²
* Stable body weight within the three months preceding study enrolment (defined as ≤ 5% change)
* No previous pharmacological or surgical treatment of obesity
* Appropriate contraception and no planned pregnancy within 8 months following enrolment

Exclusion Criteria:

* Sarcopenic obesity
* Pregnancy or lactation
* Postmenopausal status
* Diabetes
* Immobility
* Personal history of malignancy
* Personal history of pancreatitis
* Personal history of major depressive episodes
* Personal history of myopathy
* Personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma
* Current treatment with metformin or systemic corticosteroids
* Prior ocular trauma
* Intraocular or corneal surgery
* Laser refractive surgery
* Corneal nerve-affecting disease such as neurotrophic keratitis
* Active contact lens wear
* Inability or unwillingness to comply with the protocol
